newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chamber exonerates Nazi-era deserters.
newsitem.headline: German chamber exonerates Nazi-era deserters.

text.p: Germany's upper house of parliament declared on Friday that convictions for desertion during the Nazi era were not valid and called on the government to compensate deserters and their relatives.

The Bundesrat resolution, which does not have the force of law, said such convictions had been "unjust from the very beginning" and "were not verdicts of independent judges but were acts of a system of terror".
"The Budesrat calls on the government to ensure the victims and their relatives are compensated," said the resolution,

Historians estimate at least 20,000 people were executed during the Third Reich for desertion, conscientious objection or damaging morale in the armed forces, a background text accompanying the motion said.
The accompanying text stressed the motion did not mean all members of the Nazi armed forces who did not desert were supporters of a system of terror.
